title: Why You Would Die Without Sleep (And Nobody Knows Exactly Why)
description:
Tonight you'll climb into bed, turn yourself off for eight hours, and do the single most dangerous thing you do every day — sleep. You have to. If you don't, you die.

For thousands of years we had no idea why we slept. Rats kept awake for two weeks die. A seventeen-year-old once stayed up for eleven days straight and started hallucinating that he was a football player and that street signs were people.

Now we know sleep isn't downtime. It's when your brain runs its nightly cleaning crew (the glymphatic system), flushing out toxic proteins like beta-amyloid that build up to Alzheimer's. It's when memories get filed from temporary inbox into long-term storage — which is why all-nighters before exams don't work. It's when REM sleep strips the emotion off traumatic memories so you can remember them without reliving them.

Five hours a night for a week leaves you as impaired as being legally drunk. Caffeine doesn't fix it. Sleeping in on the weekend doesn't fully fix it. And eight hours straight? That's actually a modern invention — before electric light, most people slept in two four-hour chunks with an hour awake in the middle.

Sleep isn't a luxury. It's janitorial work, filing, therapy, and maintenance. Skip it and every part of you gets worse. So tonight, put the phone away. Your brain has a lot of cleaning to do.
